# Stepper

`Stepper` shows how far something has progressed through a fixed sequence of steps: the steps of a [wizard form](../patterns/form-wizard.md), the stages of an approval flow, the quality gates of a project. You give it the steps and one `progress` value saying how far the flow has got; it works out how each step looks.

It only displays progress. The page owns `progress` and decides what happens when a step is clicked. For local wizard navigation, `useStepper` manages that state; for server-owned approval stages or quality gates, keep passing `progress` directly.

## Import

```tsx
import { Stepper, useStepper } from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";
```

## Basic Usage

<example-preview name="basic-usage"></example-preview>

```tsx
function BasicUsage() {
  return (
    <Stepper
      aria-label="New purchase order"
      steps={[
        { id: "supplier", label: "Supplier" },
        { id: "delivery", label: "Delivery" },
        { id: "approval", label: "Approval" },
        { id: "review", label: "Review" },
      ]}
      progress={{ state: "in-progress", currentStepId: "delivery" }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Wizard navigation with `useStepper`

`useStepper({ steps, initialStepId? })` returns `steps` and `progress` to pass to `Stepper`, plus navigation actions. It starts at the first step unless `initialStepId` is supplied. Inline definitions preserve literal ids without `as const`: both `initialStepId` and `moveStep` only accept ids from `steps`.

<example-preview name="wizard-navigation"></example-preview>

```tsx
function WizardNavigation() {
  const flow = useStepper({
    steps: [
      { id: "supplier", label: "Supplier" },
      { id: "delivery", label: "Delivery" },
      { id: "approval", label: "Approval" },
      { id: "review", label: "Review" },
    ],
  });

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      <Stepper
        aria-label="New purchase order"
        steps={flow.steps}
        progress={flow.progress}
        onStepClick={flow.moveStep}
      />
      <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
        <Button variant="outline" disabled={!flow.canBack} onClick={flow.back}>
          Back
        </Button>
        <Button variant="ghost" disabled={flow.isComplete} onClick={flow.skip}>
          Skip
        </Button>
        <Button disabled={flow.isComplete} onClick={flow.isLastStep ? flow.finish : flow.next}>
          {flow.isLastStep || flow.isComplete ? "Finish" : "Next"}
        </Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

| Action                            | Behaviour                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `next()`                          | Complete the current step and advance; on the last step, complete the flow                                |
| `back()`                          | Go back one step; after completion, reopen the last step                                                  |
| `skip()`                          | Skip exactly the current step and advance; on the last step, complete the flow with that step skipped     |
| `finish()`                        | Complete the last step and the flow; throws if called before the last step                                |
| `moveStep(id)`                    | Move to an existing step; forward moves complete the steps passed                                         |
| `moveStep(id, { skipped: true })` | On a forward move, skip the current step and every step before the destination, excluding the destination |

For example, moving from `supplier` to `review` with `{ skipped: true }` skips `supplier`, `delivery`, and `approval`. Without the option, all three are complete. Skip records before the departure point are preserved. Backward moves discard skip records at and after the destination, so revisiting and completing a skipped step replaces its skipped status. The option has no effect on backward moves.

`currentStepId` identifies the current step, or is `undefined` once complete. `currentStepIndex` is zero-based and equals `steps.length` once complete. `isLastStep`, `isComplete`, and `canBack` support button labels and disabled states. `back()` at the first step and `next()` / `skip()` / `finish()` after completion are no-ops.

The hook requires non-empty steps with unique ids and throws for unknown initial or destination ids. Step ids and their order must stay fixed for the hook's lifetime; labels, badges, and descriptions can change. `initialStepId` is read only on mount. Remount the owner (for example with a React `key`) to reset the flow or change its sequence.

Navigation does not validate forms or submit data. Call the actions only after page-level validation succeeds, as in the [wizard form pattern](../patterns/form-wizard.md).

## Props

| Prop          | Type               | Default    | Description                                                                                   |
| ------------- | ------------------ | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `steps`       | `StepperStep[]`    | -          | The steps, in order                                                                           |
| `progress`    | `StepperProgress`  | -          | How far the flow has got (below)                                                              |
| `onStepClick` | `(id: Id) => void` | -          | Makes passed steps (completed or skipped) clickable — for example to go back to a wizard step |
| `aria-label`  | `string`           | "Progress" | Accessible name for the list of steps (the default is translated)                             |
| `className`   | `string`           | -          | Additional CSS classes                                                                        |
| `style`       | `CSSProperties`    | -          | Inline styles                                                                                 |

### `StepperStep`

| Field         | Type                | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | `Id extends string` | Stable, unique id, used by `progress` and passed to `onStepClick`                            |
| `label`       | `ReactNode`         | Step name                                                                                    |
| `badge`       | `ReactNode`         | Shown beside the label — for example a "Next" or "Overdue" `Badge`                           |
| `description` | `ReactNode`         | Shown under the label — a short hint, or a few lines of values such as plan and actual dates |

## Progress

`progress` is one of three states. Steps don't carry a status of their own, so a Stepper can't show two current steps or a completed step after the current one.

```ts
type StepperProgress<Id> =
  | { state: "not-started" }
  | { state: "in-progress"; currentStepId: Id; skippedStepIds?: Id[] }
  | { state: "complete"; skippedStepIds?: Id[] };
```

| `state`         | How the steps look                                                                |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"not-started"` | All upcoming                                                                      |
| `"in-progress"` | Before `currentStepId`: complete (or skipped); at it: current; after it: upcoming |
| `"complete"`    | All complete (or skipped)                                                         |

| Look     | Marker                         |
| -------- | ------------------------------ |
| Complete | Filled, with a check           |
| Current  | Outlined in the primary colour |
| Upcoming | Outlined, muted                |
| Skipped  | Dashed outline, muted          |

The current step gets `aria-current="step"`, and screen readers hear how the others stand ("Completed", "Skipped", "Not started"). The line is filled up to the current step, or all the way once complete.

### Skipping steps

`skippedStepIds` names steps the user moved past without doing, for example by pressing "Skip" in a wizard. Only steps already passed can be skipped: those before `currentStepId`, or any step once `complete`. A skipped step stays clickable through `onStepClick`, so the user can go back and do it.

Business states such as "Waiting for approval" or "Overdue" aren't progress; show them with `badge` or `description`.

### Typed ids

Step ids are typed from `steps`: `progress` only accepts those ids, and `onStepClick` receives them.

```tsx
<Stepper
  steps={[
    { id: "supplier", label: "Supplier" },
    { id: "review", label: "Review" },
  ]}
  progress={{ state: "in-progress", currentStepId: "review" }} // "supplier" | "review"
  onStepClick={(id) => goTo(id)} // id: "supplier" | "review"
/>
```

Steps built at runtime can't be checked by types. The Stepper warns in the console about an unknown or duplicate id, or a skipped step that hasn't been passed, and ignores it.

## Stage progress

Badges and descriptions turn the Stepper into a stage tracker on a detail page:

<example-preview name="stage-progress"></example-preview>

```tsx
function StageProgress() {
  return (
    <Stepper
      aria-label="Quality gates"
      steps={[
        { id: "qg1", label: "QG1", description: "Done 11 Aug" },
        { id: "qg2", label: "QG2", description: "Done 6 Sep" },
        { id: "qg3", label: "QG3", description: "Skipped 2 Oct" },
        {
          id: "qg4",
          label: "QG4",
          badge: <Badge variant="outline-info">Next</Badge>,
          description: "Plan 18 Nov",
        },
        { id: "qg5", label: "QG5", description: "Plan 9 Dec" },
      ]}
      progress={{ state: "in-progress", currentStepId: "qg4", skippedStepIds: ["qg3"] }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Narrow containers

The Stepper adapts to the width of its container, not the viewport:

- When the steps don't fit side by side, the row scrolls sideways rather than squeezing the labels.
- Below 400px it shows only the markers and lines, with "Step 2 of 4" and the current step's label underneath. This is what a wizard needs in a dialog on a phone.
- Each marker then names its step in a tooltip on hover, and the marker of a passed step becomes the button that goes back to it, so keyboard users still have one visible place to focus.
